If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerkâ€™s office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speakerâ€™s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.

6.  Proposed Speed Feedback Signs for Installation on Via Del Monte and Other Locations
  in the City

On motion of Humphrey, seconded by Rea, Council approved Proposed Speed Feedback Signs for
Installation on Via Del Monte and Other Locations in the City by unanimous oral vote.

AYES:  Bird, Goodhart, Humphrey, Perkins, Rea
NOES:  (None)
ABSTAIN: (None)
RECUSED: (None)
ABSENT: (None)

Director Rigg ongoing traffic concerns over the years various solutions to get speeds acceptable
level on Via Del Monte; staff directed staff to find speed feedback signs on VDM and other streets
in the City. They remind drivers they are speeding; CTE researched variety of companies; 5
presented for consideration this evening. Looking at pole mounted signs; he and cTE Fortel
(showed a speed limit sign) it is same size; letters are 12 inches and is one of the smaller signs and
matches the size of hte speed limit size. He said the Fortel sign takes 4 diff speed measurements of
each car coming forth; final reading adjacent to the sign. Data recorded by the sign; provides delta -
measures how mch the car is slowing down as it approaches the sign. It can turn off at night;
battery powered. Price is $4000 with upgraded battery; references, including LADOT and
Fullerton highly recommended. Intiailly on VDM and moved to various locations. 1-3 months,
charge, and move to another location. A policy can be developed later based on resident requests.
Vendor in Southern California.

Councilmember Perkins asked about the battery life; if solar what would be replacemtn cost. Rigg
said mfg. said +80 lbs. solar battery; relocation is more difficult. Confirmed these are recharged
batteries; Allan didn't know how many rechargings. Pole mounted; how works logisitically. Rigg
said they'd be placed on standard wood poles (40lb), or a steel channel post. Will try the wood
posts first.

MPT Goodhart asked if the device would be nonfuntional while charging; Allan said they would
charge overnight when not in use. He hoped it would last one month between charges. Then pull
sign, charge, and move it to another location. MPT Goodhart asked about evening hours; he
encouraged leaving it at night. Rigg said residents treasure views at night and was significantly
concerned they'd have complaints; it is a delicate balancing act. We are buying theswe becauswe
they're more compact; the trailer mounted signs take an hour to install; they are vandalized when
left at night.

Post would be secured in the ground with locking bolts.Speakers:

Brent Flynn, 601 VDM, thanked CC taking street problem seriously - volume and speeds. Hoped

Nahlu Ardalijian, 576 VDM, did not support an increase of speed limit. Speed humps on via Del

considering increase in speed limits this evening. Tonight the purchase of the two speed feedback
signs.

Frank Brajevich, primary concern is safety; advocate any device that calms and slows down the
traffic.

Daniel Crane, 572 VDM, favored anything slows down cars; but would like kinder gentler speed
bumps. Supported speed feedback signs as a reminder to drivers.

Linda Flynn, 601 VDM, supported speed feedback sign, but not with moving it; would rather it be
permanent.

Councilmember Rea asked what is theory of portability. Director Rigg said the expectation over
time is that they are reminders and over time there is more severe impact; it is acommon proactice
with these types of signs. If we did want to move them, if VDM calmed enough; the original itent
at least for first year on VDM. Councilmember Humphrey said diff locations on VDM; Rigg, yes,
but could be moved elsewhere if given direction.

Councilmember Perkins said data colltected how is its use envisioned? Rigg said they would report
to TSC and CC for further direction as to moveing them.

Mayor Bird asked what speeds are reflected...continual as car approaches.

Humphrey said this is a good idea and see how it goes. Councilmember Rea agreed with staff
report as suggested. Also encouraged PVE Pace Program. Councilmember perkins concurred; this
isa great next step and suppported approval as recommended by staff; it is a good choice.

 Goodhart said this will be versatile enough to meet our needs and small enough. He said they dont
want to leave any stone unturned; it is a reasonable approach to slow traffic down. Speed limit
changes are not considered this evenign but did nto promote increasing the limit. favored approval.

Only the purchase of these signs are being considered - reiterated by Councilmember Humphrey;
call City Hall to confirm what is on agenda.
